newsitem.title: THAILAND: New school year big business for Thai pawnshops. [CORRECTED 09:52 GMT]
newsitem.headline: New school year big business for Thai pawnshops. [CORRECTED 09:52 GMT]

text.p: Students aren't the only ones sharpening their pencils before the Thai school year begins.
Pawnshop owners are also doing their sums as they enjoy booming business from parents trying to scrape together enough money to pay their children's school fees.
Apart from valuables like gold teeth, parents pawn everyday objects like shoes, jeans and even imported whisky ahead of the new school term starting in May, a research report said.

The Thai Farmers Bank Research report said pawnshops traditionally boomed in the weeks before the new academic year as parents needed money to pay for school fees, uniforms and textbooks for their children.

The report said people borrowed 50 billion baht ($1.92 billion) from 387 (corrects from 140) pawnshops across the country in 1996. Eighty percent of the money was borrowed in the days leading up to the opening of school.
The trend of parents borrowing from pawnshops to pay school expenses was expected to be even higher this year due to the slump in the economy, the report said.
"Other than gold necklaces, and other valuables, gold teeth, blue jeans, shoes, imported whisky and cooking appliances are among the objects left in pawnshops as collateral," it said.
